context: Proof. By Lemma 5 the λ-theory T is axiomatised by {M = I : M ∈ Iωη } and the λ-theory T ′ by {M = I : M ∈ I η }. We have T ′ = λη, because T ′ ⊢ 1 = I and λη ⊢ M = I for every M ∈ I η . Moreover, T ′ is strictly contained into T, because every M ∈ Iωη \ I η has no βη-normal form, and therefore M = I cannot be proven in T ′ . ◀ We conjecture that the theory T of the previous proposition is strictly contained in H∗ . Proposition 7 is central to determining invertible elements modulo λ-theories. In a F -inverse monoid S, the minimum group congruence σS collapses all idempotents in the σS -class of the unit 1, so every t ∈ S becomes invertible modulo σS with inverse t∗ . Since maximal elements are canonical representatives of σS -classes, they form a group under t · u = (tu)m , which is isomorphic to S/σS by Lemma 21. It is then natural to ask what σS corresponds to in the λ-calculus. 4.1 Hereditary permutations and the theory H∗ Two λ-terms are equal in H∗ whenever their Böhm trees coincide up to infinite η-expansions [6, Thm. 16.2.7]. We denote by ≤ηω the preorder on B such that T ≤ηω U holds precisely when U is obtained from T by performing countably many possibly infinite η-expansions [7, Def. 11.11]. Moreover, we denote by nf η! (T ) the Nakajima tree of a Böhm-like tree T [7, Def. 2.60]. One calculates nf η! (T ) by eliminating from T all finite and infinite η-expansions.

paper_title: Groups and Inverse Semigroups in Lambda Calculus
statement: 5 Related and further work Inverse semigroups were first employed in the λ-calculus to study properties of β-reduction [18]. Subsequently, they played a role in Girard’s Geometry of Interaction [27]. More recently, Goubault-Larrecq, inspired by the work [18, 19], has shown that a category constructed from an inverse semigroup models a fragment of linear logic [28]. Hofmann and Mislove employed the theory of inverse semigroups to prove that every compact Hausdorff topological model of λ-calculus is degenerate [30]. We have shown that the theory of inverse semigroups improves our understanding of the interaction between invertible and idempotent elements, which is essential for characterising λ-terms invertible modulo λ-theories. Looking ahead, we aim to characterise elements that are invertible modulo λ-theories lying strictly between H+ and H∗ . The role played by E and Efin in H∗ and H+ , respectively, is taken on by other well-behaved semilattices of idempotents of PT. We conjecture that there exist λ-theories between H+ and H∗ whose group of invertible elements is strictly between FHP and HP.
